name: Cascadia

setup.text: Put all Wildlife Tokens in the cloth bag and shake it.
Count out Habitat Tiles at random without looking at them, shuffle them into face-down stacks and box the rest.
Pick 1 Wildlife Scoring Card at random for each of the five animals and lay them where everyone can see. For a first game use the cards marked A.
Deal each player one Starter Habitat Tile at random, face up. Box the others.
Turn 4 Habitat Tiles face up in the middle.
Draw 4 Wildlife Tokens and pair them, in order, with the 4 tiles.
Put the Nature Tokens within reach.
The player who most recently saw one of the game's animals goes first, or choose at random.

turn.summary: Take one tile-and-token pair and add both to your environment.
steps: Check for overpopulation first: four matching tokens are replaced automatically; three matching tokens may be replaced if you choose, once per turn.
Take one of the four pairs. Or spend a Nature Token to take any tile with any token, or to replace any number of tokens.
Place the tile and token in your environment.
Refill the row with a new tile and a new token.

end: The game ends when there is no face-down tile left to replace the one just taken. Every player takes exactly 20 turns.

scoring.text: Score each animal by its Wildlife Scoring Card.
For each of the five habitats, score 1 point per tile in your largest connected area.
Largest area bonus per habitat: 2 points; if tied, 1 point each. Nothing for second place.

Largest area bonus per habitat: 3 points, and 1 point for second largest. Two players tied for largest get 2 each and nobody scores second. Three or four tied get 1 each. Ties for second score nothing.
1 point for each unused Nature Token.

tiebreak: Most Nature Tokens; if still tied, the win is shared.

missed.text: Four matching tokens must be replaced, and this can happen several times in one turn.
Replacing three matching tokens is optional and allowed only once per turn.
Replaced tokens go back in the bag only after all replacements are finished.

not_covered: Solo mode has its own setup and scoring.
